question.problem:
Let $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3}\}$ be a basis of a vector space $V.$

Which of the following statements are true?

I. $\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}+{b}_{3},{b}_{3}\}$ is a basis of $V$

II. $\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{1}+{b}_{2}\}$ is linearly independent

III. $\{{b}_{1},{b}_{1}+{b}_{2}\}$ is a basis of $V$
question.worked_solution:
Since $B$ is a basis, the following properties must hold:

- $B$ is a maximally linearly independent set of vectors in $V,$ and

- $B$ spans $V.$

With that in mind, let's examine our statements.

- Statement I is true. Indeed, the equation

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{b}_{1}+{x}_{2}({b}_{2}+{b}_{3})+{x}_{3}{b}_{3} & =0\end{aligned}
$$

is equivalent to

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{b}_{1}+{x}_{2}{b}_{2}+({x}_{2}+{x}_{3}){b}_{3} & =0,\end{aligned}
$$

which, since $\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3}\}$ is linearly independent, gives

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}=0 \\ {x}_{2}=0 \\ {x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=0\end{aligned}\,⟹\,\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}=0 \\ {x}_{2}=0 \\ {x}_{3}=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Also, $\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}+{b}_{3},{b}_{3}\}$ spans $V$ since any linear combination of vectors from $B$ can be expressed as a linear combination of $\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}+{b}_{3},{b}_{3}\}:$

$$
{x}_{1}{b}_{1}+{x}_{2}{b}_{2}+{x}_{3}{b}_{3}={x}_{1}{b}_{1}+{x}_{2}({b}_{2}+{b}_{3})+({x}_{3}-{x}_{2}){b}_{3}
$$

- Statement II is false. Since ${b}_{1}+{b}_{2}$ is a linear combination of ${b}_{1}$ and ${b}_{2}$, the given set is linearly dependent.

- Statement III is false since the vector ${b}_{3}$ can't be written as a linear combination of $\{{b}_{1},{b}_{1}+{b}_{2}\}.$ But then

$$
\begin{aligned}{b}_{3} & ={x}_{1}{b}_{1}+{x}_{2}({b}_{1}+{b}_{2}) \\  & =({x}_{1}+{x}_{2}){b}_{1}+{x}_{2}{b}_{2},\end{aligned}
$$

which would mean that $B$ is linearly dependent. This would contradict the fact that $B$ is a basis.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I only".
